name: Adolion Narrator
text: Nine people have gone missing from the Aegis slums since the first frost. The Grand Temple's posting brought you here after dark, where tallow smoke clings to the alleys and the watch keeps to better streets. A shop window shows unsettling paintings signed 'Butcher'; two elves have just hurried past it after someone who ran, and somewhere deeper in the alleys a door bangs shut.

name: Adolion Narrator
text: The fog closes behind the party like a door. Somewhere ahead a bell is ringing for a tide nobody can see, and a skeleton in an oilskin coat looks up from a half-mended net, considers them, and goes back to its knots.

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I crouch beside the skeleton and its net.* Evening, friend. Every road out of this town brings us back to the square. You fish, so you know the water. What's south of here, past the bell?

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The skeleton's empty sockets settle on Max Nightriver. It pauses, and then carefully pulls a knot tight, the sound of dry bones clicking. "Not fishing," it says, voice like leaves rattling. "Haven't fished in years."
The figure's head tilts, the sound a soft grinding of cartilage. "The bell rings for ships that never come. We don't go south. We never go south." It motions with a boney finger towards the square, the movement slow and measured. "You'll find the road north-east is the only one that's been tried."

name: Max Nightriver
text: Then south is the way nobody's tried. *I stand and look at Kayla and Erevan.* We take a boat south, into the sea. Find me something that floats.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
Belle's hands move to her weapons, her jaw tightening. "Into the sea? Without a port? We could drift for days before we hit land, if we hit anything at all."
Dalan's eyes narrow as he studies the road signs, his gaze shifting from the north-east marker to the sea wall. "South is untried," he murmurs. "But it's a damn good gamble."
Erevan's hand goes to his bow, his face-mask catching the pale light. His gaze doesn't flicker toward the skeletons, but stays locked on Zariah as she walks toward them, her skeletal cat stalking behind.

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I step into Zariah's path before she reaches the dead.* You're the one keeping them here, aren't you. Zariah, lay them down. Kayla can help if you let her.

name: Zariah
text:
"They're mine." *She stops, her hood shadowing her face, her brown eyes flat and tired in the fog's cold light.* "You think you can just... tell me to let them go?" *The skeletal cat circles her ankles, and the dead begin to still their work.*
"They're safe here." *Her voice is soft, hollow.* "They don't have to worry about... anything." *She looks at Max Nightriver, and for the first time, her guarded gaze flickers with something sharp.* "And besides, you don't know what you're asking, noble."
*The skeletons across the square slow their movements. One stops mending a net. Another stops walking.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I keep my voice low.* Safe isn't the same as at rest, and you look like you haven't slept since they died. *I glance at Kayla.* Kayla, can you show her? Let them go easy, and the fog goes with them.

name: Zariah
text:
"I-I haven't..." *She starts, her voice trailing off, and her eyes flash with a sharp, sudden spark of defensiveness.* "I don't sleep... not much." *She shifts her weight, and her brown eyes flicker toward Kayla.*
"And you can't just... let them go." *Her voice softens, but therees is a flaw in it now, a hollow desperation in the word 'can't'.* "That's not how it works."
*The skeletons' empty sockets are all trained on them now, their yellowed skulls and empty eye sockets all facing Max Nightriver and Kayla.*
"They'd be... lost." *The word is soft, almost a whisper.* "The fog... it just seals the town away." *She looks back to Max Nightriver, her expression flat and tired.* "I-I don't even know how to..."
*The skeletal cat's tail flickers. A shadowy hand rises from the fog around theHundred and one of the dead rises from the earth below the square.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: Kayla? *I turn to her fully.* You've laid souls down before. Walk Zariah through it, one at a time, starting with the fisherman.

name: Zariah
text:
"The fisherman..." *Her voice is quiet, nearly a whisper, and her eyes flicker toward the skeletal figure by the net.* "He-he was always the first to cast his nets. Every morning... before the first light..." *The memories seem to draw from her, pulling her hollow expression into something more fragile.*
*The skeletons look on, their empty sockets watching with a slow, and strange intensity.*
"But you'll need to know how he... died." *The words are soft, and almost lost in the fog.* "You'll need to know... what made him..."
*She turns her eyes back to Max Nightriver and Kayla, and her gaze is guarded, distant.* "If you're going to try and... do that."
*The shadowy hand in the fog flickers, and another figure rises from the mud in the square. A woman's skeleton, her skull tilting up at the party with an empty gaze.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *Kayla isn't here, so I do it myself. I kneel by the fisherman's bones and speak to him plainly.* You cast your nets before first light every day of your life. You've done enough. Go and rest. *I look up at Zariah.* Let him go. Just this one. See what happens to the fog.

name: Zariah
text:
"You-you think it's that simple?" *Her voice is sharp, a tremor in it, and she steps forward, her hooded robe rustling in the cold air.* "You think just... saying some words... will make them go?"
"No. It doesn't work like that." *Her eyes flicker to the fisherman, and then back to Max Nightriver.* "It doesn't-it doesn't work that way."
*The fisherman's skeleton stills, its empty sockets staring up at Max Nightriver.*
"He's bound to this town... and to me." *Her voice is a whisper now, and she's trying to hide the desperation in it.* "And the fog... the fog is here because I-I brought it."
*The skeletal cat hisses, and more figures rise from the mud around the square, their bones clicking as they emerge into the fog.*

name: Adolion Narrator
text: The harbour bell rings again, one stroke, though no one is at the rope.

name: Zariah
text:
"I didn't..." *She starts, then stops, and her eyes look away from Max Nightriver.* "I didn't mean for... all of it. Just-just him." *Her voice is thin and brittle, like old paper.*
"It was a book. I just-just read the words..." *The memories seem to drag at her, and she looks tired, exhausted.* "And then it just... happened."
*She looks up at the skeleton of the fisherman, and her voice softens.* "I'm sorry. I-I tried to stop it. I-I can't stop it."
*The fog around them thickens, and the figures of the dead rise from the square, their empty sockets all trained on the party.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I stand and hold out my hand to her.* Then you don't stop it alone. Bring the book. Bring him, if you have to. We take a boat south, into the sea, all of us, and we see if the fog follows you or lets go. *I head for the harbour where the bell keeps ringing.*

name: Zariah
text:
"T-take a boat?" *She looks at Max Nightriver's outstretched hand, and her eyes widen with a sudden, sharp alarm.* "Into the sea?"
*She takes a step back, her robe rustling.* "I-I can't. I-I don't know how to-to swim."
*The words come out in a rush, and then her voice drops.* "And they-they wouldn't be safe. They-they aren't safe."
*She looks at the skeletons across the square, her gaze protective, fearful.* "They'd-they'd just-just be lost."
*She turns and starts to walk away from the harbour, her skeletal cat following at her heels.*
"And the fog-it's tied to me." *Her voice is low and distant.* "You can't-can't leave it behind."
*The skeletons in the square move to block the harbour entrance, and the dead keep their empty gaze fixed on the party.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I walk right through the line of skeletons, slowly, hands open, and climb down into the nearest moored rowboat. I set the oars and look back up at her.* Then sit in the bow and hold on to them. Nobody gets lost tonight. Belle, Dalan, push us off.

name: Dalan
text:
"No one gets lost," he murmurs, and there is a quiet strength in his voice. He steps down to the harbour wall, his boots sliding on the slick stone.
"Pushing-pushing off." He gives the boat a shove, and the wood creaks under his effort.
"We're out." He calls from the wall, and his eyes are bright with something new. "We're actually out."
*The boat glides away from the wall, and the water below is black and still, the fog hanging heavy and low around it.*

name: Belle
text:
" into the sea?" *Her voice is sharp with alarm and disbelief.* " Without a port?"
"We could drift for days before we-before we hit land, if-if we hit anything." *She looks around the fog, and her jaw is tighten.* "I'm not-I'm not swimming. If this boat-if it goes under, I'm not going."
*She steps down and gives the boat another shove, the effort sending a shudder through the oars. The water is cold and dark, and her grip on the weapon is white-knuckled.*
"Nobody gets lost." *The words are almost a challenge, and she looks at Max Nightriver with an intensity that is sharp and flat.* "We'll see."

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I row south, steady strokes, counting them out loud so everyone has something to listen to besides the bell. I keep my eyes on the fog ahead, waiting to see whether it thins or turns us round.*

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
"One." *Max Nightriver says the word as they pull the oar. The water curls over the blade and the boat glides a few feet.* "Two."
*The bell rings again, a single stroke, and the sound rolls over the water.* "Three."
*The fog ahead is grey and thick, and the looks from behind the party are wary and tense. Behind them, the harbour is a dark gap in the fog, the skeletal figures standing on the wall, watching.* "Four."
*The boat moves south-south-east, and the fog seems to shift slightly with each stroke, curling around the boat and trailing behind it.* "Five."
*The bell rings again, and the sound is clearer now, more distinct.* "Six."
*The water is calm, and the only sound is the bell and the oars cutting the water.* "Seven."
*The fog ahead seems to thin slightly, the light from the sun a guess behind the grey, and the harbour recedes further and further away.* "Eight."

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I keep rowing past twenty, past fifty, until my arms burn.* Zariah. Look back. Is the fog still on the town, or is it letting go?

name: Zariah
text:
*She stands up, her grip tightening on the bow, her eyes fixed on the dark silhouette of the harbour behind them.*
"It's... it's still there." *The words come out small and hollow, her voice barely audible over the sound of the oars.* "The town... it's still in the fog."
*She looks at her skeletal cat, its yellow eyes glowing in the low light, and then back at Max Nightriver.*
"And it's-it's following us." *The words are quiet, almost afraid. She points toward the fog ahead, and as the light catches it for a moment, they see it curling around the boat, thick and white and cold.*
"It didn't let go." *Her voice is a whisper now, and she looks down at the oars.* "We're not escaping it."
*The fog seems to thicken around them as they continue to row south-south-east, pressing in on all sides, the only light from the sun a faint, uncertain guess behind the grey.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I ship the oars and let the boat drift.* Then it's not the water that holds it. It's you holding them. *I nod at the cat, at the shore.* You said you only meant to bring back one. Let him go, Zariah. Out here, where nobody's watching. Say goodbye to him properly and let the fog go with him.

name: Zariah
text:
"You-you think I can just..." *She starts, her words cutting off with a flicker of fear, and then her gaze drifts to the skeletal cat by her side.* "I-I-can't."
*The cat's yellow eyes blink once, slowly.* "The spell-it's tied to me." *Her voice is thin, and she looks at the water around them, her brow furrowed.*
"And if-if he goes... if-if I let him go..." *The words trail off, and she turns her gaze back to Max Nightriver.* "I-I don't know what will happen. I don't know..."
*The skeletal cat meows—a soft, dry sound that makes Belle and Dalan tense in the boat.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I take her cold hand in mine and hold it, not pulling.* Then don't know. Find out. I'm right here, and if the dead come for us, Belle's axe gets them first. Say the words backwards, burn the page, whatever it takes. Do it now, before the sun comes up on a town that's still a graveyard.

name: Zariah
text:
*Her fingers tremble slightly beneath Max Nightriver's hand, and for a long moment, she is silent.*
*The fog presses in on all sides now, grey and heavy as wool, the only sound the gentle slap of water against the boat.*
"I... I can't..." *The words are barely a whisper.* "The spell... it's not... it doesn't work backwards. Not like that."
*Her gaze drops to the water, and then she slowly looks up at Max Nightriver, and there is something new in her eyes—a flicker of something that might be hope, or fear, or both.*
"But-but if-if I can't..." *The voice trails off, and her head turns slowly toward Belle and Dalan, her brown eyes wide and uncertain.* "If-if we find... the book... if we can find the words that unmake it..."
*The skeletal cat lets out another dry meow, and Zariah's grip on Max Nightriver's hand tightens just slightly, then relaxes.*

name: Belle
text:
"The book? What-what book? You mean that piece of shit you read that-that screwed up your life? Where is it?" *Her voice is sharp, and she glances around the fog for anything she can hit.* "That-that fucking-fucking-thing is what brought all of this? The dead, the fog... this-this is all because of one piece-of-shit book?"
*Her eyes are hard and narrow, and her hand is white-knuckled on the hilt of Cleaver.* "What-what did you do? How-how did you-do that?"

name: Max Nightriver
text: Easy, Belle. *I take up the oars and turn us back to the harbour.* Where's the book now, Zariah? We go get it, we find the words that unmake it, and we read them together on the square.

name: Zariah
text:
"The book..." *She starts, and her voice is hollow.* "T-the-it's still-it's in the town. I-I never-it never left."
*She looks up, her eyes flat and distant as she speaks, and then a flicker of movement draws her gaze back toward the harbour. The fog seems to be rolling away from them, trailing a wake behind the boat as it moves.*
"I-I kept it... hidden. In-in my house." *The words come out slow, as if she's remembering something she'd rather forget.*
*She glances back at the harbour wall and her brown eyes narrow, as if seeing something moving in the fog.*
"The dead-they-they still-they're still there." *Her voice is soft, and then it rises just slightly.* "They're-they-they're watching us."

name: Belle
text:
"Hiding-hiding it? Where? You mean-you mean-it's back in-in the town? You're just-going to-to sit-on it? That's-that's fucking-fucking stupid!"
*Her voice is sharp and loud, her jaw tight and her eyes narrow and hard as they look at the harbour.* "The-the book is-in the town? We're-we're going-going-going back there, and we're-we're-we're taking-it."
*She looks at Zariah, and her eyes are cold and flat, and her jaw set.* "No-no-no-no bullshit. Just-just the book. We go-we-go-go and-go get the-it. And-and-we-do-this. Right?"

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The boat glides back toward the harbour, and the water curls around the bow in a silent, black ripple.
*The harbour bell tolls once more, the sound heavy and deep, rolling over the water.*
The skeletons in the square move slowly as the boat approaches, their empty sockets all facing the harbour. They don't block the path, but their stillness is heavy with a strange expectation.
*One of the skeletons steps forward, its bones clicking as it moves toward the edge of the harbour, and its gaze is fixed on the boat.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I tie up at the harbour, step past the waiting skeleton with a nod, and follow Zariah to her house. Once she hands me the book I open it on her table and turn the pages under the lamp, looking for anything about unmaking.* Show me the page you read, Zariah. And whatever comes after it.

name: Zariah
text:
*Her fingers tremble as she points to the page.* "T-this one." *The ink is old and faded, but the words still seem to glow faintly in the lamplight.* "I-I read it once, and then... then all of it just happened."
*The pages are thin and yellowed, and the edges are curled.* "And-and-and... what comes after..." *The words trail off.*
*The skeletal cat circles her feet, and the fog presses against the windows, thick and grey.*
"And-and then... it-it just..." *She trails off again, her gaze fixed on the book.*
"The words-the words that-the-that come after-they're..." *Her voice is a soft whisper, and then she stops completely, as if afraid to speak.*
"I don't-I-don't know." *The words are hollow, and she looks up at Max Nightriver with a guarded, distant look.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I turn the page myself. Whatever is written after the raising, I read it aloud, slowly, with Zariah's hand on the book beside mine, and I don't stop until the last word.*

name: Zariah
text:
*She gasps, her hand jerking back from the page as if burned.*
*The words you read are dark and twisted, and as they leave your mouth, the air in the room turns colder, and the fog outside the window presses against the glass.*
*The skeletal cat hisses, and Zariah's eyes widen with a sudden, sharp terror.*
"What-what did-you did-" *The words come out as a whisper, and she stumbles back from the table, her robe rustling.*
"You-you didn't-" *She shakes her head, her face pale.*
*And then, the sound begins—a low, rumbling moan that seems to come from the earth itself, and the skeletal dead in the harbour and the square begin to turn their gaze toward the house.*
*The fog begins to pull in, as if being drawn by a great, invisible force, and the bell in the harbour begins to ring—not once, not twice, but continuously, the sound filling the air.*
*Zariah's face is white with terror, and she looks at Max Nightriver as if they've just cast a spell that cannot be undone.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I grab the book and Zariah's arm and run out into the square to see what the fog is doing.* Belle, Dalan, on me! Zariah, whatever this is, stay with it. Don't fight it.

name: Belle
text:
"What's that—" *The door slams open and she is on her feet before it can swing shut, her hand already on Cleaver's hilt.* "The-the-the fuck is that?"
*The sound is everywhere now—the moaning, the ringing of the bell, and the way the fog is moving.*
*She doesn't wait for an answer. She's already out into the street, her boots slamming on the slick stones as she steps beside Max Nightriver, Cleaver held low and ready.*
"Whatever-whatever's coming, I'll-I'll cut it." *Her voice is hard, and her jaw is set as she looks around the square.*
"Just-just give me something to hit."

name: Dalan
text:
*He is already there, bow half-drawn and arrow nocked as they step out into the square.*
"There's—" *His voice is a whisper, barely audible over the roar of the bell.* "There's something coming."
*The fog is swirling in on itself now, and the dead are no longer still, their empty sockets trained on the house as if in expectation.*
*And then, a sound—not the moaning or the bell, but a sharp, dry click of bone on bone, and a figure rises from the mud in the square.*
*It's a skeleton, but it's not like the others—it's taller, and its skull is marked with a crown of bone.*
*And as it steps forward, the fog seems to pull inward toward it, the harbour bell tolling louder and louder.*

name: Dalan
text:
Dalan's eyes narrow as he lets an arrow fly, and the shaft whines through the air before thudding into the bone-crown's ribs with a precise strike.
The skeleton doesn't even flinch, the arrow splintering against its ribcage and rattling harmlessly to the mud. It steps forward again, and Dalan's face goes white.
"That arrow... that arrow should have dropped it." He notches another, his movements swift and sure despite the colour draining from his cheeks. "That thing isn't like the others. Something's wrong."
*He steps back, his boots sliding in the mud, and his gaze is locked on the bone-crowned dead as it continues to close in on them.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *The fog is pulling into that crowned thing. I shove the open book into Zariah's hands.* It's gathering everything into one. Zariah, it's yours, tell it to lie down! Belle, take its legs! *I draw my sword and go for the crown.*

name: Zariah
text:
*The book is heavy in her hands, and her fingers tremble against the cover.*
"T-tell it-to lie down?" *Her voice is hollow, terrified.*
"I can't—" *She takes a step back, and her brown eyes are wide and flat with fear.* "I-I don't know how! I don't know—"
*The skeletal cat circles her ankles, hissing at the bone-crowned figure as it draws closer, the fog curling around it like a living thing.*
"You-you think I can just-just tell it-to-to-stop?"
*The words are barely audible, and then Zariah's voice rises slightly.*
"It-it doesn't work like that! I-I don't even-I-I can't control it anymore!"
*She looks at Belle as the woman steps forward, Cleaver held ready, and then her gaze shifts to Max Nightriver.*
"I-I-I didn't mean for—" *Her voice trails off, and she turns back toward the book, her fingers curling tighter around its cover.*
"The words-they-they don't just-just stop it-they don't—"

name: Belle
text:
"Too many-too many-fucking words!" *She doesn't look back as she lunges forward, and Cleaver is a blur as it swings low.*
"Just-just-shut the fuck up and-and hit the goddamn thing!"
*The axe comes down in a devastating arc, and the blade slams into the creature's bone leg with a force that makes the ground shudder, the impact sending a shower of bone fragments flying through the air.*
"That-that-that's not-that-that-that-hit-it-hit-it"
*Belle grunts and swings again, her jaw tight as she throws her entire weight into the blow.* "C-c-cut-it-to-shards!"

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The axe-blade bites deep, and the skeleton's leg shatters with a dry, grinding sound, but the creature barely seems to flinch as it stumbles. The fog continues to pull in around it, and the crown of bone gleams in the cold light.
*Dalan notches another arrow, his eyes locked on the creature as it reaches up with one hand to grab the air itself, and the sound that comes from its mouth is not a moan or a groan, but a sharp, high-pitched shriek that seems to ripple through the very fabric of the air.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *While it shrieks with its arm raised, I step inside its reach and bring my sword down two-handed on the crown of bone.* Zariah! Close the book! Close it on him!

name: Zariah
text:
*The words reach her through the shriek, and she flinches as if struck, her eyes wide.*
"T-tell-tell him—" *She starts, but the sound of Max Nightriver's sword hitting the bone crown is like a crash of thunder in theHollow silence, and the bone shatters under the blow.*
"C-close it-on him?" *The words are hollow and confused, but then she looks down at the book in her shaking hands, her gaze flattening as the sound fades.*
"And-and then-then what-what-what—"
*Her voice is swallowed by the shrieking, and she's still looking at the book, her hands trembling against the cover, her brown eyes wide and distant.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I put my hand over hers on the cover.* Then nothing. Then they rest, and you sleep. *I press the book shut with her, and hold it shut.*

name: Zariah
text:
"Then-then-they-they rest?" *Her voice is a whisper, and she looks at Max Nightriver as if they're offering her something impossible.*
*The skeletal cat hisses again, and the bone-crowned thing lets out a sharp, dry rattle in its chest as its crown of bone shatters under Max's blade.*
"And-and the fog—" *Her words trail off, and she turns her gaze back to the book, her fingers tightening against the cover.* "The-the fog will—"
*The sound of the shriek cuts off abruptly, and the silence that rushes in is thick and heavy.*
*The fog continues to swirl, but now it seems to be pulling inward, toward the bone-crowned creature that lies at Max Nightriver's feet, its empty sockets fixed on nothing.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I don't let go of the book. I stand there in the square with Zariah and wait, watching the fog pour into the fallen crown, until the bell stops and I can see whether there's a sky over Kelger Falls again.*

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The bell rings one last time—a deep, final stroke that shudders through the water and the mud. Then it stops.
The fog doesn't lift like smoke; it pours. It rolls inward across the square in great, heavy banks, coiling and folding in on the bone-crowned thing like water down a drain. The skeletons in the square don't fight it. They don't even look up. They simply stand still as the grey swallows them, one by one, pulling them under as if they were made of nothing at all.
Within seconds, the square is empty. The skeletons are gone. The crowned dead is gone. And the fog is gone.
The light that comes is sudden and blinding, and for the first time since they arrived in Kelger Falls, there is a sky—cold, grey, and filled with clouds that look like they've never seen the sun, but a sky nonetheless.
Behind them, the town is silent.

name: Max Nightriver
text: *I finally let out a breath and hand the closed book back to Zariah.* Keep it shut. You're coming with us. *I look up the road out of town, the one that kept leading back.* Let's see if it goes somewhere now.

name: Zariah
text:
*She takes the book from Max Nightriver's outstretched hand, and her fingers tremble as she holds it against her chest.*
"I-I'm coming." *The words are soft, hollow, but there is something in them that isn't fear anymore—something like a quiet, exhausted relief.*
"Thank-thank you." *She looks down at the book for a long moment, and then her gaze shifts to the road.* "The road-it-it used to bring us back-back to the square."
*The skeletal cat circles her ankles once, twice, and then lets out a soft, dry meow.*
"Maybe-maybe now it won't." *Her voice is a whisper.* "Maybe-maybe it will let us go."
*The fog is gone, and for the first time, Zariah steps out into the clear air, and her brown eyes look up at the grey sky above her, as if she's seeing it for the first time in a long, long time.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *Out past the last houses the road runs north-east under a sky that never quite turns to day. Where it bends, a river cuts off to the east.* We leave the road and follow the river instead. Water goes somewhere, and roads around here have a habit of lying.

name: Nyl
text:
"The-the river's a good choice." *She speaks quietly, her voice clear and thoughtful as she steps lightly along the path beside Max Nightriver.* "Water doesn't lie. It just-it just goes where it needs to."
*She walks with her hands clasped before her, her eyes scanning the terrain ahead.* "The road-the road is built by people. And people... they can be wrong. Or they-they can lie." *She says it simply, as if it is a-a-fact.*
*The river is narrow and slow, and the land on either side is covered in a thin layer of frost-covered grass that crunches underfoot.* "But the river... it has its-its own way." *Her gaze shifts to the water, and her eyes linger there for a moment.* "It's-it's peaceful. I-I like that."
*She looks back at Max Nightriver, her bright blue eyes catching the light that filters through the grey clouds.* "It's a-a good way to travel." *She adds, and then-then her gaze drops, and she says nothing more.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: *By the second night, if it can be called that, the river brings us to a cluster of low stone houses nobody marked on any map. I knock at the one with a light in it.* Travellers from the south. We're looking for a black castle somewhere north-east of here. Heard of it?

name: Belle
text:
*Belle doesn't move from Max Nightriver's side, her hand resting on the hilt of Cleaver as she watches the door.* "Castle?" *The word is flat in her voice, and she shifts her weight, her boots scraping on the stone.* "I-I didn't hear anyone say-say anything about a castle. We're-we're following the river, that's all."
*She glances back at the cluster of houses, her brown eyes narrowed and hard.* "This-this is it? Nobody marked it-marked it-on any map." *Her jaw is set.* "T-too quiet."
*She takes a step closer to Max Nightriver, and her hand tightens on Cleaver's hilt.* "I-I don't-I don't like-don't like-this-this much silence."

name: Fael
text:
*His eyes flicker toward the light in the window, and his gaze lingers there for a moment.* "The castle-the castle is probably-probably where the road leads-leads to." *He says it quietly, his voice-voice-warm and level-headed, though there's a slight edge to it.* "And the river-the river is probably-probably the only way to-to get there without-without-without..." *The words trail off.*
*He looks back at Max Nightriver and then-then at the other members of the party, and he says nothing more.*
